We need answer only valid JSON with keys. Need produce concise architecture plan at most 2000 words. Need complete JSON. Need include state_machine list states/transitions, timer_plan timers required PT durations reset conditions, priorities, initial_values, scan_execution_order explicit 4-stage, formal_assertions optional list.

We need reason about spec. No timers required. state machine four states IDLE MOVING COMPLETE FAULT. Transitions per scan priority. Need reflect post-transition outputs. Need state is retained pre-state q. At each scan sample inputs, safety/reset priority & transitions. At most one state step. Need in FAULT remain until cleared by Reset without Jam. Priority: Jam true -> FAULT regardless. Reset true when Jam false -> IDLE (even if in IDLE etc), but priority says Jam first so if both Jam and Reset, Jam wins -> FAULT. If already in FAULT and no Jam? Requirement (3) if already in FAULT, remain until cleared by Reset without Jam. But requirement (2) Reset true -> IDLE. Need order: (1) Jam->FAULT; (2) Reset->IDLE; (3) if already in FAULT remain until cleared by Reset (without Jam); (4) Stop->IDLE; etc. If in FAULT, Jam false, Reset true -> IDLE (requirement 2). If in FAULT Jam false Reset false -> remain FAULT (req 3). If in FAULT Jam true Reset true -> Jam wins FAULT. If in FAULT Jam true Reset false -> FAULT. If in FAULT Jam false Reset false Stop true? Req 3 says remain in FAULT until cleared by Reset; priority Stop lower, so remain FAULT. Good.

If in any state and Jam true -> FAULT (also from FAULT remains). If Jam false Reset true -> IDLE from any state. Stop true -> IDLE if no higher (Jam false, Reset false, not qFault? But qFault with no reset and Stop true must remain FAULT due req 3; so stop doesn't override fault). For non-fault: if Stop true -> IDLE. Else qMOVING and AtExit true -> COMPLETE. Else qIDLE Start true and AtExit false -> MOVING. Else hold. What about qIDLE Start true and AtExit true: hold IDLE (blocked). qCOMPLETE hold until Jam/Reset/Stop. qMOVING AtExit false hold MOVING. AtExit true in MOVING -> COMPLETE. AtExit true in IDLE? no start because condition !AtExit. Stop in COMPLETE -> IDLE. Reset in COMPLETE -> IDLE. Jam -> Fault.

Outputs: Belt iff state MOVING post-transition; Complete iff COMPLETE; Fault iff FAULT. At most one.

Need produce formal assertions over port names. Could include list with formulas using G and q? They ask optional list of {"id","formula"} temporal/invariant assertions over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names. Need perhaps include simplified LTL using ports only. But formulas in spec use q state predicates; formal_assertions over port names maybe can include output invariants. Use only declared port names Start Stop AtExit Jam Reset Belt Complete Fault. We can include assertions like G(!(Belt && Complete)), etc. Need maybe include state-based? They asked over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names. We can include invariants that don't require state predicates? But many require state. We can express some using outputs? Need optional, so could include relevant port-only assertions: G(Jam -> (Fault & !Belt & !Complete)); G((!Jam & Reset) -> (!Belt & !Complete & !Fault)); G(!(Belt & (Complete | Fault))); G(!(Belt & Complete) & (!(Jam) -> ...? cannot express qFault). We can include G(!(Belt && Complete)), G(!(Belt && Fault)), G(!(Complete && Fault))? At most one active means all pairwise mutual exclusion, yes output at most one active. But Complete and Fault not directly in spec? at most one active implies not both. However Complete & Fault false always. Include.

Could include G(Fault -> ...?) tricky. P7 uses state. But formula "G(Fault -> (Fault U (!Jam & Reset)))" doesn't use qFault and says if Fault then remains until clear or forever? Actually G(Fault -> (Fault U (!Jam & Reset))) implies if no clear eventually violation? In LTL, strong until requires clear eventually. Spec P7 is G(Fault -> (G Fault | (Fault U (!Jam & Reset)))) handles forever. But over port names can include. Could include P1, P3, P6, P9 output part. Maybe include only safe invariants.

Need timer_plan: empty list or list stating no timers. Since required key, use []. But maybe include "timer_plan": [] and mention no PT. The schema says timers required, PT durations, reset conditions. Empty okay. Maybe include one object? Not needed. They may expect list. Use [].

Need state_machine: Could list states and transitions. Maybe array of objects:
[
 {"state":"IDLE","description":"...","transitions":[
   {"to":"FAULT","condition":"Jam"},
   {"to":"IDLE","condition":"!Jam && Reset"},
   {"to":"IDLE","condition":"!Jam && !Reset && Stop"},
   {"to":"MOVING","condition":"!Jam && !Reset && !Stop && Start && !AtExit"},
   {"to":"IDLE","condition":"otherwise (hold)"}
 ]},
 ...
]
Need ensure priority. For FAULT: transitions:
{"to":"FAULT","condition":"Jam","priority":1},
{"to":"IDLE","condition":"!Jam && Reset","priority":2},
{"to":"FAULT","condition":"!Jam && !Reset","priority":3, "note":"latched hold; Stop ignored"}
Maybe include no other.
For MOVING:
priority 1 Jam -> FAULT
priority 2 !Jam && Reset -> IDLE
priority 3? qFault no (not fault)
priority 4 !Jam && !Reset && Stop -> IDLE
priority 5 !Jam && !Reset && !Stop && AtExit -> COMPLETE
priority hold -> MOVING (condition !Jam && !Reset && !Stop && !AtExit)
But also if qMOVING AtExit true and Stop true: Stop priority -> IDLE (higher than AtExit). Good. If Reset and Stop both -> Reset priority -> IDLE same target. If Jam and Reset -> FAULT.
For COMPLETE:
Jam->FAULT
!Jam && Reset->IDLE
!Jam && !Reset && Stop->IDLE
hold COMPLETE otherwise (including AtExit? yes)
For IDLE:
Jam->FAULT
!Jam && Reset->IDLE
!Jam && !Reset && Stop->IDLE
!Jam && !Reset && !Stop && Start && !AtExit -> MOVING
hold IDLE otherwise (including Start && AtExit)
Need "at most one state step" clear. Outputs based on state post-transition.

Need priorities: safety and operational priorities list. Could include numbered with Jam highest, Reset (if no Jam), fault latch, Stop, normal transitions, outputs unconditionally derived. Also note at most one state transition per scan.

Initial_values: include state "IDLE", Belt false Complete false Fault false maybe input? initial values for variables: state, Belt, Complete, Fault. Could include q? Use:
{
 "state": "IDLE",
 "Belt": false,
 "Complete": false,
 "Fault": false
}
Maybe include Start Stop AtExit Jam Reset false? Spec only outputs and state. They ask initial values for variables. Include inputs false? Could. But initial_conditions only state/outputs. Safer include all: Start false, Stop false, AtExit false, Jam false, Reset false, Belt false, Complete false, Fault false, state "IDLE". But "state" internal. We can include.

Need scan_execution_order explicit 4-stage scan order exactly:
[
 "1. Edge sampling: sample all inputs (Start, Stop, AtExit, Jam, Reset) once at scan start; no output-dependent logic; retain pre-state q[k].",
 "2. Safety/reset priority & state transitions: evaluate priority ladder on q[k] and sampled inputs; execute at most one transition; compute q[k+1].",
 "3. Unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF: none (no timers); if timers existed, call them unconditionally here.",
 "4. Unified output assignments: assign Belt := (state= MOVING), Complete := (state= COMPLETE), Fault := (state= FAULT) after transition, all in one place."
]
They asked "explicit 4-stage scan order (1. edge sampling, 2. safety/reset priority & state transitions, 3. unconditional top-level timer FB calls outside CASE/IF, 4. unified output assignments)". Use object or list of strings. Need maybe "scan_execution_order": [ ... ].

Need formal_assertions: optional list. Include formulas. Need consider port-only. Since they specify "over declared VAR_INPUT/VAR_OUTPUT port names". Use G formulas. Could include:
A1: "G(!(Belt && Complete))"
A2: "G(!(Belt && Fault))"
A3: "G(!(Complete && Fault))"
A4: "G(Jam -> (Fault && !Belt && !Complete))"
A5: "G((!Jam && Reset) -> (!Belt && !Complete && !Fault))"
A6: "G((!Jam && !Reset && Stop) -> (!Belt && !Complete))" Wait if Fault? If Stop with qFault and no Reset, output Fault true. Formula would say !Fault? Not true. Use only for non-fault can't express. Avoid.
A7: "G((!Jam && Reset) -> (!Belt && !Complete && !Fault))" from P3.
A8: "G((Jam) -> (Fault && !Belt && !Complete))"
A9: "G(!(Belt && (Complete || Fault)))"
A10: "G(Fault -> (Fault W (!Jam && Reset)))" weak until? This says Fault persists unless clear. But if clear happens simultaneously? If Jam false Reset true and qFault, output !Fault, so at that scan clear. Formula G(Fault -> (Fault W (!Jam && Reset))) means if Fault at current, then Fault until before clear? Weak until allows clear at same? Actually W: p W q means p until q or G p. If q current, p need not hold? At current Fault true and q true (!Jam&Reset), formula true because q holds. This means fault can clear. But if Fault true while Jam also? q false. Need persist. But if Fault true at scan and next scan Fault false due reset without Jam, okay. However if Fault true and next scan q false (no reset) but output false then violation. Good. But formula uses Fault output. Could include "G(Fault -> (Fault W (!Jam && Reset)))" but note if Jam true and Reset true, q false (since !Jam false), and Fault should remain, okay. But if Fault true due Jam and next scan Reset true Jam false, q true, formula satisfied. This is okay. But they might prefer P7 exact with G Fault | U. Use "G(Fault -> (G Fault || (Fault U (!Jam && Reset))))" which is valid LTL over ports. But "G Fault" nested? okay. Include maybe not.

Need ensure JSON valid. No markdown. Need answer only JSON. Could be concise. Need within 2000 words. Fine.

Let's craft JSON with all keys. Need state_machine "list of states and transitions". Could be array of objects. Ensure no comments. Strings with ! etc. Use "&&", "||". Need be complete JSON.

Potential issue: formal_assertions formulas with "G" and "U" need escaped? No. Use strings. Use "&&" etc. All quotes escaped.

Need include "timer_plan": [] maybe with note? Could be array. If they expect timers required, PT durations, reset conditions, empty list okay. Maybe include object list with no timer? Hmm key says timer_plan: timers required, PT durations, reset conditions. Could do "timer_plan": [] and in scan stage note no timers. That's acceptable.

Need maybe "state_machine" include initial state and transitions. Let's design.

  ]
 },

 },

Need ensure in IDLE priority 3 Stop condition: if Reset false and Jam false, Stop -> IDLE. If qIDLE anyway hold. Fine. But if Stop true and Start true, Stop priority -> IDLE. Good. If IDLE Start true AtExit false and Stop false -> MOVING. If Start true AtExit true -> hold (condition false due !AtExit, otherwise hold). Good.

Potential nuance: In FAULT and Jam true and Reset true: priority 1 -> FAULT. Good.
FAULT and Jam false Reset true -> IDLE. Good.
FAULT and Jam false Reset false Stop true -> priority 3 -> FAULT. Good.

Outputs reflect post-transition. But state_machine outputs field could be misleading as outputs while in state? It's okay. But output assignments stage. Could include outputs per state.

 "4. Stop: if no higher priority applies, Stop TRUE transitions non-FAULT states to IDLE.",
 "5. Normal motion: MOVING && AtExit -> COMPLETE; IDLE && Start && !AtExit -> MOVING; otherwise hold.",
 "6. Outputs are derived only from post-transition state; exactly one of Belt/Complete/Fault can be TRUE."
]
